title: 1700 Shocks 2300 Master
informationNeeded: A PGN or complete FEN with side to move and board orientation, or clear full-board frames covering the relevant endgame.
reviewNotes: Physical-board game recap; many saved views show people, clocks or only part of the board. Narration does not specify a complete legal move sequence.
transcript: This is me, a 1700 rated player, and my opponent is a 2300 rated FIDE Master. And anything can happen indeed, because we go down this weird line of the London system, where my opponent plays c5 and b5, but I come prepared and I blitz out f3, which clearly catches him off guard and makes him start hesitating. The fact that I know this line slightly better than him allows me to win a pawn and gain a slight advantage. So, now he realizes that he needs to lock in, and he uses almost an entire minute on his next move. But I overestimate my position, and I decide to trade queens, going down an end game that is actually better for him. But suddenly, out of nowhere, he blunders a full rook to a knight fork, and he realizes right away. But unfortunately, I don't realize, so I give this check instead. Eventually, my position starts to fall apart, literally, and I'm left with no other choice but to resign the game. >> You actually win, man.
